newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russian businessman abducted in Berlin.
newsitem.headline: Russian businessman abducted in Berlin.

text.p: German police said on Wednesday a Russian businessman had been kidnapped in Berlin and his abductors wanted one million marks ($579,000) in ransom money.

Alexander Galius, 50, was abducted on June 9 from a computer shop where he worked in Berlin's Charlottenburg district after his kidnappers knocked him out with anaesthetic and carried him away unconscious, police said.

Police say they made contact with the kidnappers several times since but had not heard from them since last weekend. They gave no further details, but Berlin newspapers were rife with speculation the Russian mafia were behind the attack.

Since the collapse of the former Soviet Union in 1991 violent crime has risen sharply in Russia, and Russian police say organised mafia-style groups are responsible for many attacks on bankers, businessmen and politicians.
Bonn says there has been a rise in organised crime and blames the trend partly on mafia-groups from the former eastern bloc extending their turf to Germany.
